subject: general
question: In ancient India, the 'Vajjis' had their capital at Vaishali, which was ruled by the ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lichchhavis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Vajji** (or **Vrijji**) was one of the **16 Mahajanapadas** (great kingdoms) of ancient **India** that flourished between the **6th and 4th centuries BCE**.
 
• The capital of the **Vajji** confederacy was **Vaishali**, located in the modern-day **Vaishali district** of **Bihar**.
 
• The **Vajji** territory was governed not by a single monarch but as a **Gana-Sangha** (an oligarchic republic). The **Lichchhavis** were the most powerful and prominent clan among the **eight clans** that formed the **Vajji** confederacy.
 
• The **Lichchhavis** are historically celebrated for establishing what is often considered one of the earliest examples of a **republican form of government** in the world.
 
• In this system, the territory was ruled by many **Rajas** (kings), sometimes numbering in the thousands, who met in assemblies to discuss and debate state matters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Context of Vajjis**:

 
 
• The **Vajji** kingdom was situated to the **north of the Ganges** river. It was bordered by the **Gandak river** to the west and the **Kosi river** to the east.
 
• The region was extremely fertile, making it a prosperous agricultural and commercial center in ancient **India**.
 
 
 
• **The 16 Mahajanapadas**:
 
 
• Ancient texts like the Buddhist **Anguttara Nikaya** and the Jain **Bhagavati Sutra** list **16 Mahajanapadas** that existed during the second urbanization.
 
• These included **Magadha**, **Kosala**, **Vatsa**, and **Avanti**, which were powerful monarchies, alongside republics like **Vajji** and **Malla**.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explained**:
 
 
• **Mallas**: This was another **Gana-Sangha** located to the north of **Vajji**. They had two main branches with capitals at **Kusinara** (where **Gautama Buddha** attained Parinirvana) and **Pava**.
 
• **Kambojas**: Situated in the **northwestern** part of the Indian subcontinent (near modern **Afghanistan** and **Pakistan**). They were renowned for their high-quality **horses** and excellent cavalry.
 
• **Kurus**: Centered around the modern-day **Delhi-Meerut** region. Their capital was **Indraprastha**, and they are prominently mentioned in the epic **Mahabharata**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Religious Significance**: **Vaishali** is the birthplace of **Lord Mahavira**, the **24th Tirthankara** of **Jainism**, who belonged to the **Jnatrika** clan (another member of the Vajji confederacy).
 
• **Buddhist Connection**: The **Second Buddhist Council** was held at **Vaishali** in **383 BCE**, approximately a century after the **Buddha's** death. The **Buddha** also visited **Vaishali** many times and delivered several important discourses there.
 
• **Conflict with Magadha**: The **Vajji** confederacy was eventually conquered by **Ajatashatru**, the ruler of **Magadha**. Historians record that the war lasted for nearly **16 years**, and **Ajatashatru** used advanced military technology like **Mahashilakantaka** (a catapult) and **Rathamusala** (a chariot with blades).
 
• **Administrative Structure**: The **Lichchhavis** had a sophisticated administration with officials such as the **Raja** (head), **Uparaja** (vice-head), **Senapati** (commander), and **Bhandagarika** (treasurer).
